question: A 55-year-old man comes to the physician because of fatigue and worsening abdominal pain for 4 weeks. He also reports excessive night sweats and a 5.4-kg (12-lb) weight loss during this time. He has a neck swelling for 4 days. Physical examination shows a nontender, enlarged, and fixed supraclavicular lymph node. There is splenomegaly. A CT scan of the thorax and abdomen shows massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes. Analysis of an excised cervical lymph node shows lymphocytes with a high proliferative index that stain positive for CD20. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Fatigue and abdominal pain" -> "Weight loss and night sweats" -> "Enlarged, fixed supraclavicular lymph node" -> "Splenomegaly" -> "Massively enlarged lymph nodes on CT scan" -> "Lymphocytes with high proliferative index" -> "Positive staining for CD20" -> "Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Neck swelling" -> "Nontender, enlarged, fixed lymph node" -> "CD20 positive lymphocytes" -> "High proliferative index of lymphocytes" -> "Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Weight loss" -> "Night sweats" -> "Enlarged lymph nodes in multiple regions" -> "Lymphocytes positive for CD20" -> "Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Splenomegaly" -> "Enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes" -> "Lymphocytes with high proliferative index" -> "CD20 positive staining" -> "Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Fatigue" -> "Abdominal pain" -> "Supraclavicular lymph node enlargement" -> "Positive CD20 staining in lymphocytes" -> "Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma" -> 95%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms and findings suggestive of a high-grade lymphoma, including systemic symptoms (fatigue, night sweats, weight loss), extensive lymphadenopathy, and splenomegaly. The biopsy showing lymphocytes with a high proliferative index and positive staining for CD20 supports a diagnosis of a B-cell lymphoma. Among the options, diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) is the most likely diagnosis given the aggressive nature of the disease, extensive lymphadenopathy, and the histopathological findings. DLBCL is characterized by large B-cells with a high proliferative index, fitting the description provided.
